THE COUNT WAS RE-DERIVED, NOT QUOTED: fourth's document said twelve branches, the real figure is 89 of 98. T17 landed in the same commit because until the row lands the provenance gap is latent behind the size failure. 26 arms green from 6 passed / 13 failed / 4 unproven; ablated eight ways.

risks.basis: the same app (stonedesk) has this defect on record
risks.risk: StoneDesk's photo-to-quote visualizer listed slabs from sdSlabs, the localStorage array, filtered to status:'in-stock'. The filter is right; the input is not. slabSyncFromSupabase() runs only from loadSlabs(), behind the _slabLoaded once-per-session guard, so the picker showed whatever was cached when the app started. A slab another device reserved an hour earlier still read in-stock. THE DOUBLE SALE WAS NEVER THE EXPOSURE and that is why this looked closed: api/sd-data.js's slabs/reserve branch is a real compare-and-swap that refuses a conflict with 409 and uses a plain INSERT rather than the write branch's upsert, so two devices racing an unsynced slab collide on the unique index. What a stale list costs is a METERED render -- the panel tracks viz-kpi-used/cap/left, so a rep picks the held slab, SPENDS a render showing the customer their kitchen in that stone, and only finds out at Quote This. The money is safe; the render and the conversation are not. Fixed by awaiting the sync before listing, and by giving slabSyncFromSupabase() a {ok, reason} return so a failed or empty refresh renders the cached list WITH a line saying the reservations on it may be out of date rather than silently passing it off as current.

risks.basis: the same app (stonedesk) has this defect on record
risks.risk: StoneDesk's profit figure coerced one operand of a subtraction and not the other. de7b4838 wrapped the invoices half in Number() and left the bills half -- bills.reduce(s + (b.amt || 0)) -- untouched ON THE SAME LINE, at stonedesk.html:36531 and :36544. DRIVEN, NOT REASONED: bills of "100" and "200" fold to the STRING "0100200", so profit reports -99450 where 450 is right. A string sum inside a subtraction produces an arbitrary negative rather than merely appending, which is why this is worse than an uncoerced sum alone. BOTH CONSUMERS STATE THE NUMBER AS FACT RATHER THAN DISPLAYING IT: sdTaxCalc posts it to /api/claude as "Actual tracked data: revenue minus expenses (profit) of $X" and asks for estimated annual liability, quarterly schedule and 1099 obligations; sdTaxPrint prints it on a Tax Report where Math.max(0, profit*0.28) turns the negative into $0 rather than NaN, silently understating tax on a document a shop hands a CPA. The same function's salesTaxYTD was uncoerced too -- entries of "50" and "25" fold to "05025", which Math.round makes 5025, so $75 prints as "$5,025": not an error, a plausible wrong number two orders of magnitude out. FOUND BY INDEPENDENT REVIEW of the very commit that introduced it, while discharging that commit's Tier A obligation. Both fields were in truthy_sum_baseline.json's grandfathered map so truthy_sum_check.py exited 0 and printed CLEAN throughout; removing them immediately exposed a THIRD tax surface -- taxRender(), drawing panel-tax's KPI tiles -- with three more uncoerced folds, one of which the checker structurally cannot detect because it has no fallback at all. Six folds fixed, two baseline entries removed, and api/sd-data.js's invoices write branch now refuses a non-numeric amount with 400 INVALID_AMOUNT so the input cannot reach storage in the first place.

risks.basis: the same app (stonedesk) has this defect on record
risks.risk: stonedesk.html's Admin Overview 'Storage Used' KPI computed Math.min(100, Math.round((totalBytes/1024/5120)*100)) and wrote it into a card labelled only 'Storage Used'. THE FLAGGED Math.min IS THE ONE PART THAT WAS RIGHT and is recorded as a FALSE POSITIVE for the overrun-inversion class: a localStorage quota is a hard ceiling, a write past it throws, so the ratio cannot legitimately exceed 1 and the cap could never hide an overrun. The two real defects were beside it. (1) THE DENOMINATOR WAS ASSUMED: 5120 KB is a guess at the browser quota, real quotas vary by browser and origin, and where the true quota is larger this reported a half-used store as FULL -- a number an owner acts on, by deleting data, from the two delete buttons on the same panel. (2) THE POPULATION WAS NOT THE ONE THE LABEL NAMED: the loop sums EVERY key in localStorage, which on this platform is every SAIRN app in the browser, and presented it as StoneDesk's -- while the paragraph eleven lines below the card draws exactly that distinction for the delete buttons ('removes only what StoneDesk stored -- other SAIRN apps in this browser are untouched'). So the card showed a percentage of a guess over another app's data. Fixed to report the measured bytes with the label naming the population; the percentage returns when navigator.storage.estimate() is wired with a real quota rather than a constant. Regression suite written first with a known-bad control that restores both halves in a copy and requires two arms red, file restored byte-identical.

risks.basis: the same app (stonedesk) has this defect on record
risks.risk: stonedesk.html's Admin Overview storage KPI reported bytes as if they were exact after the invented 5MB percentage was removed earlier the same day. Two things were still wrong with the figure. (1) `.length * 2` assumes two bytes per UTF-16 code unit, which is wrong for an astral character (a surrogate pair is two units) and is not how every engine charges its quota, so the total is an approximation presented as a measurement. (2) THE KEYS WERE NOT COUNTED AT ALL -- only the values -- and keys are stored too, so the figure was biased DOWN, which is the wrong direction for a number somebody reads as 'how full am I'. Keys are now included and the value carries a `~`, a mark on the number rather than a longer label because the card has room for a figure and not a sentence. AND THE QUOTA SEARCH IS RECORDED SO IT IS NOT REPEATED: no storage_quota, storage_limit, quota_bytes or max_storage exists anywhere in the repo's .js, .sql, .json or .html, and vercel.json carries no storage configuration. It would not help if it did -- this KPI counts BROWSER localStorage, which neither Supabase nor Vercel governs, and the browser's own limit varies by engine and origin and is not knowable synchronously. So no percentage is computed and none is invented.

risks.basis: the same app (stonedesk) has this defect on record
risks.risk:
slabSyncOne and sdLineageSyncOne reported a LANDED write as lost. Both decided
whether the write reached the server by testing sdData()'s return value against
null, and that value is the unwrapped `data` key. api/sd-data.js answers
`data: (Array.isArray(rows) && rows[0]) ? rows[0].data : payload` on 69 write
branches -- the guard is on the ROW existing, not on its jsonb blob being
non-null -- so a stored row whose `data` column is null comes back as 200 /
ok:true / data:null, sdData unwraps it to null, and both functions fall through
to `return false` and warn that the yard copy and the server copy now disagree
about a record that is sitting on the server. The fix reads the envelope instead:
_sdWriteOk[resource] is set false on sdData's first line and true only after the
j.ok test passes, and sdWriteLanded(resource) returns it with a strict === true
so a call that never happened is false rather than undefined.
